facts.text: Józsefváros was renamed in 1777 after Emperor Joseph II, the heir to the Hungarian throne.
The district houses the National Museum, the oldest museum in Hungary, and the Metropolitan Ervin Szabó Library inside the 19th‑century Wenckheim Palace.
The historic Pál utca, Mária utca and Füvészkert botanical garden are the real locations where Ferenc Molnár’s classic novel The Paul Street Boys was set.
Gutenberg tér and Rákóczi tér were once brick‑factory hubs, reflecting Józsefváros’s industrial past in the 19th century.
The district’s eastern railway station and the nearby Kerepesi Cemetery, Hungary’s most famous cemetery, sit close to the residential core.
Corvin‑Szigony Project, the largest urban renewal effort in Central Europe, is reshaping Józsefváros’s 19th‑century housing stock.
